How it works

Skins Game: players draft all 30 NBA teams and root for each team's WINS or its LOSSES. Every time your chosen outcome happens (e.g. you picked losses for the Spurs and they lose), you get a skin. Whoever has the most skins at the end of the regular season wins. This season is a three-player league (Eristeo, Brian, Adam) with 10 teams each.

Skins % 2023-26
58%, 62%, 59%, 59%
Winner's skins %
61%, 68%, 65%, 66% (6-player leagues; with 3 players each roster is a third of the league, so expect this year's winner to finish with a lower %)
Skins % projection
Each team's current skins % × 82, added up: where a player finishes if every team keeps its current rate.
Weighted avg
Vegas 40%, TR 20%, ESPN 20%, CBS 20% (most accurate robust blend on 2025-26 Oct-Nov data; until CBS publishes: Vegas 50%, TR 25%, ESPN 25%). A missing Vegas line is carried forward for up to 5 days.
BB-Ref, Opta, DARKO, D&T, Crafted
Shown and graded for accuracy but not in the weighted average. Opta (The Analyst), DARKO, Dunks & Threes and Crafted NBA are on trial in 2026-27 and may join the blend next season if they prove accurate.
Chance to win
10,000 simulated seasons around the weighted average. It narrows as more games are played. Uncertainty is based on 25% this season's projection misses (16 games per team so far; capped at 25%), 75% last season's. Each simulated season plays out every remaining game on the schedule (965 games left on the schedule (60 team-games not yet scheduled, played vs a league-average side)): team strengths are set so each team's expected final record matches its weighted-average projection, with a home-court edge, and every game has one winner and one loser. The spread combines game-to-game luck in the games left and the chance the projection misjudges the team (currently 8.5 wins over a full season, shrinking as games are played); player totals are then summed across their 10 teams. Teams on the same roster can miss together, as they did last season: roster correlation 0.25 (the floor; last season's was 0.30), applied from opening night (0.25 in use now). The Best guess view uses 7.4 wins and correlation 0.15, the values 24 past seasons support; the default is wider on purpose.

About these numbers

Skins % projection = each team's skins % × 82, added up. Projected rows are final-season skins from each source; bold = best in the row. Avg = league average per player. Toggle to Skins % to see the share of a player's 820 games each projection implies. Skins % projection can sit a little off the actual Skins % because it averages each team's rate equally, while Skins % counts every game played, and teams have played different numbers of games.

About these numbers

Average miss in wins per team, grading only games played after each projection was saved (opening night: Oct 20, 16 games per team; last 30 days: since Oct 22, 15 games per team). Lower is better; best source in bold. The .500 baseline shows how much the projections beat a coin flip.

What the number means: for each team we take a projection, work out how many wins it expected over the games played since, and compare that with the wins the team actually got. The gap is the miss. The table shows the average miss per team, in wins, so 1.50 means the source was off by about one and a half wins per team over that stretch. Only games played after the projection was saved count, so no source gets credit for results it already knew. The .500 baseline simply assumes every team wins half its remaining games; a source has to beat it to be adding anything.

Since Oct 27 grades every source over the same games, starting the first day all of them had a projection for the whole league. That is the fairest side-by-side: the since-opening column gives the sources added later (*) fewer, easier games.

Tiers: with only 30 teams and a few weeks of games, small gaps are luck. Tier 1 sources cannot be told apart from the best one (the bold number); Tier 2 sources are behind the best by more than luck explains. Tiers use the last 30 days column. A dash means too few teams to judge. Most sources land in Tier 1 early; the split sharpens as games pile up.

Early-season sample: with only about 10 games per team, gaps of a few hundredths between sources are mostly noise. Read it as a rough first look; it firms up as games pile up.

  • Not tracked on opening night; graded since its first saved projection (BB-Ref: Oct 22; Opta: Oct 21; DARKO: Oct 21; Dunks & Threes: Oct 21). Opta, DARKO, Dunks & Threes and Crafted NBA are tracked for accuracy only and are not in the weighted average.

Suggested weights (best fit across all 9 sources, graded since Oct 27, about 12 games per team): ESPN BPI 90%, CBS 10% — miss 1.74 vs 1.78 for the Weighted Average (current weights: TeamRankings 20%, ESPN BPI 20%, CBS 20%, Vegas 40%) and 1.85 averaging all 9 equally. These cover only the games since Oct 27, when every source had a projection, so they run lower than the since-opening column above. With 30 teams and this few games the best mix is mostly luck, so gaps this small are not a reason to change the weights yet.

League skins % outlookwhere the league total should finish

So far: 63.8% of games earned a skin (300 of 470, 19.1% of the season). The pre-game Vegas moneylines (no-vig consensus) implied 60.4% for the same games, so the league is running +3.5 points (about +16 skins) above the market.

W picks 63.7% vs 60.3% expected (237 games); L picks 63.9% vs 60.4% expected (233 games).

How to read this

Tap a header to sort. Projected W/L are final-season records from the chosen source; Average is the mean of every source that has the team. The projection list is ordered by accuracy so far (average miss in wins, from Projection accuracy above). Seed = rank within the conference by projected wins (ties broken by current record); NBA rank is the same across all 30 teams. Seed range and Proj W range show the best and worst case across the individual sources. Status: seeds 1–6 playoffs, 7–10 play-in, 11+ lottery.

About these numbers

Playoff %, play-in %, seed, draft slot and 1st-pick % are from ESPN's BPI projections (espn.com/nba/bpi). The lottery-ball and bottom-3 odds are from Basketball-Reference's projected draft order (10,000 simulations of the rest of the season). Both are saved once a day and neither site keeps history, so each chart starts the day it was first saved.
